clue.text: Scanty result as little money's put in hat

indicators.note: put in tells us the small coin goes inside the headgear word

parts.note: a lid is slang for a hat
a mite is a tiny coin, as in the widow's mite

explanation.surface: A meagre outcome when only a few coins are dropped into a collecting hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited supplies are restricted or meagre, a synonym of scanty.

clue.text: Former PM's point in support of drunkard?

indicators.note: in a down clue, in support of puts the compass point beneath the drunkard

parts.note: drunk as a lord is the saying, so a lord is a playful drunkard
north is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A past prime minister's point is backing up a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick North, Lord North, led the British government from 1770 to 1782.

clue.text: Soldiers attempt to capture a river in battle

indicators.note: to capture means the soldiers' letters enclose the other pieces

parts.note: men are soldiers, other ranks
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Troops try to seize a river during fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go inside MENGO, splitting it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Marengo was Napoleon's 1800 victory over the Austrians in northern Italy.

clue.text: Revolver needed to take singular advantage

explanation.definitionFit: A record deck's rotating platter is a thing that revolves; and to turn the tables, put in the singular, is to gain the upper hand.

clue.text: Fishy lot may give detective clue

explanation.definitionFit: Dabs are small flatfish; in slang, dabs are fingerprints, evidence for a detective.

clue.text: Cryptic clue an anagram? Right

indicators.note: the word anagram openly tells us to rearrange the neighbouring letters

explanation.surface: A solver asks whether a puzzling clue is an anagram and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: 'anagram' rearranges CLUE AN to UNCLEA, and R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cryptic is obscure in meaning, as is anything not plain to understand.

clue.text: Idle at school? One's prepared to act when necessary

definitions.text: One's prepared to act when necessary

explanation.definitionFit: Studying too little is a comic reading of under-study; an understudy is an actor ready to stand in.

clue.text: Paradoxical father of Wordsworth's man

parts.note: the poet wrote that the young one is father of the adult, a paradox

explanation.walkthrough: From Wordsworth's 'My Heart Leaps Up': 'The ... is father of the Man.'
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's line makes the young offspring parent to the grown man, a famous paradox.

clue.text: Old country seat collapsed on one inside

indicators.note: inside places the other pieces within the rearranged seat
a seat that has collapsed is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old chair gave way when someone sat on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges the furniture word, and 'inside' sets the two short pieces within it, three letters in. 'Old' fits because the country was then part of the USSR.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia was an independent Baltic republic before 1940, so when this was set it was a former country.

clue.text: Kitchener's series of mounts:

explanation.definitionFit: A range is a kitchen stove, so belonging to a kitchen; and a range is a chain of mountains.

clue.text: Kings are held to be less like common folk

indicators.note: held means the kings' letters grip the next word between them

parts.note: R is short for Rex, king, so two kings are RR

explanation.surface: Monarchs are thought to be set apart from ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare can mean uncommon, so the comparative describes someone further from the ordinary run of people.

clue.text: China has poor start in game

indicators.note: start places the word for poor at the beginning of the piece

parts.note: poor quality is bad
Minton is a famous make of English porcelain

explanation.surface: Chinese porcelain gets off to a weak beginning in some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is porcelain: MINTON, a Staffordshire pottery firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a net is a game.

clue.text: Number of Romans in excess

parts.note: the Roman numerals XC are what you hear at the start of excess, said as ex-cess

explanation.walkthrough: Romans wrote this number as XC, and 'excess' begins with the sounds of those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman numerals ninety is written XC, which the opening of the word excess spells out in sound.

clue.text: Female discretion

explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is a woman's name, and it also means careful good judgment, a synonym of discretion.

clue.text: Red and pink potted? Comes out all square

explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a red scores one and the pink six, a break worth seven; to end with neither profit nor loss is to come out even.

clue.text: Greek character leads doctor a diamond

indicators.note: leads puts the Greek letter in front of the doctor

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A Greek man guides a physician to a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb is a rhombus, the equal-sided slanted shape known as a diamond.

clue.text: Logical basis for the French being on desert island

indicators.note: being on means the French article comes after the other pieces

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray
Iona is a Scottish island in the Hebrides
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone justifies being French while stranded on a desert island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert island' reads as one phrase, but 'desert' is the verb RAT and 'island' is IONA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning that underlies an action, its logical basis.

clue.text: Selected as secondary activity

explanation.definitionFit: A player picked for a team is in the side; something done as a sideline is a secondary pursuit.

clue.text: Superheat mixture using large current

indicators.note: mixture tells us the letters of the word are stirred together

explanation.surface: Overheating a blend of something produces a strong flow.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of Mesopotamia is a large current of water.

clue.text: One to employ in home, having lost last help

definitions.text: One to employ in home, having lost last help

indicators.note: in places the word for employ inside the dwelling word
having lost last tells us the dwelling word drops its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
to employ something is to use it
aid means help

explanation.surface: A domestic servant one hires for the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost last' trims the dwelling word to HOM before 'in' sets the verb inside it. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic servant engaged to clean in a household is someone you employ at home who helps.

clue.text: Inexperienced, and lacking judgment

explanation.definitionFit: Someone untested is raw; a case never heard in court has received no verdict.

clue.text: Fill to the brim — to drop litter?

explanation.definitionFit: To replenish a glass fully is to fill it again; and to pup is to give birth to a litter of young dogs.

clue.text: Beneficiary of patronage got peer in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A favoured young person landed a nobleman in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is someone supported and promoted by a patron.

clue.text: Reinforce Scot's outer room with lock

parts.note: in a Scottish two-room cottage, the but and ben, the but is the outer room
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A Scotsman strengthens his front room with a new door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door fitting but is a lock of hair. In Scots, a 'but and ben' is a two-room cottage; the 'but' is the outer room.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttress a wall is to prop it up, a synonym of reinforce.

clue.text: Northern woman capable of making clean sweep

explanation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect a besom is a disparaging term for a woman; it is also a broom made of twigs.

clue.text: Severely criticizes conclusion reached by 17

indicators.note: conclusion reached by means only the closing part of the answer to the other clue is kept

parts.note: the answer to clue 17 down

explanation.surface: Someone harshly attacks the finish arrived at by a fellow solver.
explanation.walkthrough: The last five letters of the 17-down answer are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is to scold them angrily, an old sense of the verb.

clue.text: Painter about to add colour in France

parts.note: re means about or concerning
noir is French for black

explanation.surface: An artist is ready to add a French shade to the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Hunting brother taken in by tent-dweller

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this skilful hunter was tricked out of his birthright by his brother Jacob, described as dwelling in tents.

clue.text: My destination when I encountered polygamist

definitions.text: My destination when I encountered polygamist

parts.words: My destination when I encountered polygamist
parts.note: the nursery rhyme speaker was going to a Cornish town when meeting a man with seven wives

explanation.walkthrough: From the rhyme 'As I was going to ...', in which the speaker meets a man with seven wives. The town is in Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old riddle-rhyme the narrator is travelling to this Cornish town when the much-married man appears.

clue.text: Famous date — first in Tacitus that is written in full

parts.note: the Ides of March, when Caesar was killed, is a famous date

indicators.note: first in takes just the opening letter of the historian's name

explanation.surface: A celebrated date is the first thing to appear in a Roman historian's writings.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation i.e. stands for two Latin words; the clue asks for them spelled out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase abbreviated i.e. means that is, here given unabbreviated.

clue.text: US President's in capital of state

explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth American President, and the capital of Wisconsin bears his name.

clue.text: Ineffective way to save

explanation.definitionFit: Something useless achieves nothing; read as two words, using less is a way to economise.
